Channeled spectropolarimetry measures all four Stokes parameters (S₀, S₁, S₂, S₃) using a single spectrum by amplitude modulating them onto spectral carrier frequencies.
The paper was published in Optical Engineering, Volume 49, Issue 5, May 2010, with DOI 10.1117/1.3430565.
Aliasing occurs when high-frequency spectral features like narrow-band atomic absorption lines extend the S₀ centerburst to higher OPD values, creating false polarimetric signatures.
The false-signature reduction technique (ART) requires two measurements: one with the analyzer at 0 degrees and another at 90 degrees.
ART produces a 180-degree carrier frequency phase shift relative to conventional CP measurements, enabling removal of S₁, S₂, and S₃ when measurements are weighted and summed.
The MWIR experimental setup uses yttrium vanadate (YVO₄) retarders with thicknesses d₂ = 4 mm and d₁ = 2 mm (2:1 ratio).
YVO₄ retarders exhibit appreciable dichroism between approximately 3.5-5 μm wavelengths.
The MWIR system operates over a ±5-degree field of view.
Seven distinct frequency channels are present in the interferogram, separated in OPD space by phase retardances φ₁ and φ₂.
The reference beam calibration technique requires measuring known polarization states at 22.5-degree intervals to demodulate phase factors.
When dichroism is present, an improved calibration procedure requires reference data at both 0-degree and 45-degree linear polarization states.
Dichroism produces cross-talk between CP channels and creates residual signatures that modulate S₂ and S₃ by the phase term φ₁.
CdS retarders operate over approximately 2-15 μm wavelengths and use a 2:1 thickness ratio with d₂ = 10 mm and d₁ = 5 mm.
The commercial Oriel MIR8000 FTS system uses an 80026 MCT detector and 80007 Silicon Carbide source.
A 2:1 afocal beam reducer is used in the MWIR setup to improve system throughput through the relatively small clear aperture of YVO₄ retarders (~12 mm).
Full-resolution S₀ reconstruction is achieved with ART because S₀ can be isolated for all measured OPD values, not just near the centerburst.
Spectral resolution of the S₀ Stokes parameter is improved up to the maximum resolution offered by the spectrometer using ART.
The theoretical model for ART implementation on a Fourier transform infrared spectrometer includes an enhanced model accounting for dichroism within the crystal.
Misalignment of the analyzer prevents achievement of the perfect 180-degree carrier frequency phase shift, resulting in residual S₀ components in the channels.
The paper presents experimental results demonstrating ART across wavelengths spanning 2.5-15 μm using different crystal retarders.
Conventional CP reconstructions make use of a single-scan measurement, which is not ideal due to aliasing between adjacent carrier frequency channels.
The Stokes parameters are implicitly dependent on wavenumber (σ̃), defined as σ̃ = σ⁻¹.
The phase terms in the system are implicitly dependent on wavenumber and are determined by the birefringence of the crystal and retarder thicknesses.
The paper addresses the significant reduction in aliasing errors that can be achieved if knowledge of the S₀ component (the centerburst) can be obtained.
Filtering algorithms are required to remove residual S₂ and S₃ modulations produced by dichroism in the dual-scan interferogram.
